statement: Use the trapezium rule with 4 strips to estimate $I=\int_{0}^{1}e^{-x^{2}}dx$. (ii) The true value is about $0.7468$; find the error of the estimate. (iii) Explain whether the estimate over- or under-estimates.
solution: (i) $h=0.25$. Points $x=0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1$ with $f=e^{-x^{2}}$: $1,\ e^{-0.0625}\approx0.9394,\ e^{-0.25}\approx0.7788,\ e^{-0.5625}\approx0.5698,\ e^{-1}\approx0.3679$. $T=\frac{0.25}{2}(1+2(0.9394+0.7788+0.5698)+0.3679)\approx0.7430$. (ii) Error $\approx0.7430-0.7468=-0.0038$. (iii) The estimate is an underestimate. (The function is concave near $0$ where the trapezium lies below the curve, and the overall effect is an underestimate.)
hints: Compute the function at the 5 equally spaced points.
Compare with the known true value.
